audit.why: Both layers give Urgot all seven rows and the packet levelChart agrees (Urgot x7) at a 54.44% win rate over 529 games. The ratings also taper sensibly — 8/10 through the early levels, 6/10 at his Lich Bane spike — rather than sitting flat, so the chart is internally honest.

audit.why: Spikes are named and timed: his level-6 Purgatory, Q max at 9, and the Lich Bane first item against your bruiser item and the level-6 execute. The E cooldown quoted in report[7] and breakdown.cooldowns ('a 10-second timer') matches the kit exactly — E is a flat 10s at every rank.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single biggest interaction in the matchup is absent: Purgatory GROUNDS. Every field describes it only as an execute zone, so nothing warns you that Disdain will not fire while you stand in it — which is exactly the moment you would reach for your escape.
audit.why: Urgot's E is his only gap-closer and his only exit, and Corrosive Charge carries movement too. Being grounded at low health inside an execute zone is the death sequence this page is supposed to prevent, and it never says the word.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now states the grounding alongside the floor; dontsFull[2].d rewritten from a duplicate of tradeBad into the actual Purgatory threshold rule.
sources: enemyKit R grounding flag: 'shuts off enemy dashes'
ownerKit E and Q dash flags

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t says 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.'
audit.why: Soul Ignition heals him for a portion of the self-damage at the end of the effect. That is still a heal, and Grievous Wounds reduces it — the distinction between a refund and lifesteal does not exempt it. Telling the player to skip anti-heal costs them exactly the extended trades the ability is built to win.
audit.corrected: Rest of the item line kept (the Zhonya's-beats-the-execute point is good); the anti-heal sentence replaced with the real rule.
sources: enemyKit W text and heal flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Two Do/Don't bodies do not match their own titles: dosFull[2] is titled 'Break off fights before the Purgatory floor' but its body is about wasted nail recasts, and dontsFull[2] is titled 'Coin-flip at low HP inside his totem zone' but its body is a verbatim copy of tradeBad about nail marks.
audit.why: The reader gets a heading promising the Purgatory rule and a body that never delivers it, twice — so the one thing that kills them is stated nowhere on the card.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to say what their headings promise.

notes: This page is far better written than the templated ones and needed little: the chart, the spikes and the E cooldown all check out against the kit. The one real hole was Purgatory's grounding, which appears nowhere despite being the mechanic that turns 'low HP in the zone' into a guaranteed death for a champion whose only exit is a dash. Locke has no Data Dragon entry (packet.enemyAbilities is null), so ability NAMES could not be verified: the kit text confirms 'Soul Nails' as the Q projectile and the missing-interactions file gives Silver Stake (P), Soul Ignition (W) and Ashen Pursuit (E), but 'Ritual Nails' (Q) and 'Purgatory' (R) as used throughout this page are unverified — I left every one of them alone rather than guess. Likewise the repeated '125 range' claim about Locke is not in any data I have and was left untouched.
